conditions: The declared input schema requires a structured step and already has typed refusal semantics.
construction: Validate the original value before construction, return the existing typed refusal for unsupported shape and preserve valid input behavior.
description: Repair structured ingress with explicit typed refusals while preserving valid normalization.
example: if not isinstance(raw_step, dict): return Err(RefusalRecord(code="BAD_STEP", reason="Step must be a mapping"))

lesson.applicability: A declared structured-step or ingress contract rejects scalars, malformed mappings or invalid collection members.
lesson.cause: The parser substitutes its own request for the caller request and loses the failure witness.
lesson.correction: Apply the existing structured-input validator and return the named typed refusal for unsupported values.
lesson.counterexample: AP_PY_013 documents a scalar converted into a nullary operation and mixed-list items discarded without refusal.
lesson.evidence_excerpt: Any malformed structure (such as unexpected scalars, malformed step dictionaries, or unrecognized elements) triggers an immediate, typed refusal record without silent transformation or data dropping.
lesson.exceptions: Preserve documented valid normalization, supported optional fields and existing refusal vocabulary. Do not tighten unrelated schemas.
lesson.failed_claim: Silently converting or discarding malformed inputs preserves a structured workflow request.
